assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity with selection into exporting (Melitz 2003; Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple 2004) reorganised both theory and empirics of international trade. It introduced new channels for gains from trade and became the standard framework for micro-data work on firms, trade and policy. The influence is broad and durable.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is the originator of the core heterogeneous-firm model, and Helpman has the broadest set of foundational contributions, including the FDI-versus-exports margin. Redding is a major contributor to quantitative trade and spatial models, but his work is more a later extension and is less central to this specific discovery, so I leave him out.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of confirmation and wide empirical use. Trade has not been recognised since 2008, so timing is favourable.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would prefer a three-person split that adds Redding or Bernard-Jensen-style empirical pioneers, who are not on this ballot.
Helpman may be seen as better paired with Grossman (B047) for a different trade citation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities, Calvo pricing, the Taylor rule and the micro-founded New Keynesian framework underpin modern monetary policy analysis and central-bank practice worldwide. The impact on both academic macroeconomics and policy is exceptional.
assessment.attribution: The credited list is large and the credit is spread. Calvo (1983) and Taylor (1980 staggered contracts, 1993 rule) are the clearest origins of the pricing and rule building blocks. Woodford synthesised the framework and its normative policy implications. Gali, Gertler, Christiano and Eichenbaum, and Smets are very strong, but the three-laureate cap forces a choice.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of confirmation and heavy real-world uptake, and fully mature. Some of the 2008 crisis-era critique is acknowledged, but the framework has been extended rather than displaced.
uncertainties: Attribution is contestable because several equally credible contributors are excluded.
Whether the committee would split the credit between the pricing/rule foundations and the DSGE estimation line.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kiyotaki-Moore (1997) shows how collateral constraints and asset prices amplify and propagate shocks. It is a foundational mechanism for credit cycles and a core building block of macro-finance, with clear relevance to financial crises and policy.
assessment.attribution: The core contribution is cleanly attributable to Kiyotaki and Moore. Gertler and Gilchrist are important for the related financial-accelerator and empirical lines, but the ballot's core discovery is the collateral-constraint mechanism. Related financial-friction work by an earlier laureate is outside the list.
assessment.maturity: Nearly three decades of citations and extensions, and the framework is now standard in macro-finance.
uncertainties: The overlap with Bernanke-Gertler accelerator work, and with the 2022 financial-intermediation prize, could be read as partial redundancy.
Empirical identification of the collateral channel is less conclusive than the theory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based view of technology and wage inequality, together with the China-shock evidence on local labour-market adjustment, transformed how economists and policymakers think about automation, trade and distribution. The credibility of the empirical design and the policy influence are both high.
assessment.attribution: Katz is central to the long skill-bias and education-versus-technology literature. Autor leads the task and polarisation work and the China-shock papers. Hanson co-led the trade-shock evidence. Dorn is an important co-author but more junior. Attribution is reasonable, though the three come from two overlapping bodies of work.
assessment.maturity: The task framework dates from the early 2000s and the China-shock papers from 2013 onward. They are well replicated and extended, though some quantitative interpretations are still debated.
uncertainties: Partial overlap with the 2024 prize on institutions and with Acemoglu's technology work.
Debate over the size of the China-shock effects and their long-run persistence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rubinstein's 1982 alternating-offers model is the canonical non-cooperative solution to bargaining, and the Rubinstein-Wolinsky market extension links bargaining to decentralised trade and search. It is the standard foundation for bargaining in game theory, labour and matching models.
assessment.attribution: The founding result is Rubinstein's. Wolinsky is the clear second through the market-bargaining work. Binmore's contributions to the strategic foundations and the Nash programme are important but follow the core result.
assessment.maturity: More than forty years of confirmation, with deep integration across subfields. Bargaining theory itself has not been the explicit citation of an earlier prize.
uncertainties: The committee may see game theory as already heavily recognised by previous prizes and prefer applied-impact areas.
Rubinstein's own methodological scepticism does not bear on merit, but it adds timing uncertainty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hsieh-Klenow (2009) offered a measurable framework linking within-industry misallocation of inputs to aggregate TFP, and showed that it explains a substantial part of cross-country income differences. This is a major shift in growth and development accounting, with strong policy relevance.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow are the authors of the central framework and its empirical implementation. Restuccia's closely related work is largely co-authored with someone outside this credited set, which weakens a clean three-person attribution.
assessment.maturity: About fifteen years of use, with a very large follow-on literature. The measurement approach is influential, though it remains contested.
uncertainties: Measurement error in the underlying data and the sensitivity of the TFP gains to model assumptions.
Whether the committee judges it mature enough relative to older candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A systematic theoretical and empirical programme on how electoral rules, constitutions and state capacity shape fiscal policy and economic outcomes. It helped establish modern political economics as a core field.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the central pairing through their constitutional and electoral-rule research, and Besley contributed major work on accountability and state capacity. The three together are a coherent set, though credit is shared with institutional-economics research the committee has recently recognised.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty-five years of work and a mature literature. Some causal identification in cross-country constitutional studies remains debated.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 institutions prize may reduce the marginal case.
The cross-country empirical results are more fragile than the theory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bayesian persuasion (Kamenica-Gentzkow 2011) provides a tractable framework for designing information structures to influence decisions, and it has spread rapidly through theory, market design, regulation and platform design. It is conceptually elegant and has broad applications.
assessment.attribution: Kamenica and Gentzkow originated the Bayesian persuasion model. Bergemann and Morris developed the closely related information-design and robust-mechanism framework, so credit is divided, and the three-name cap excludes one of those lines.
assessment.maturity: A relatively young literature of about fifteen years. Its theoretical influence is clear, but empirical or institutional confirmation is thinner than for older candidates.
uncertainties: Whether the committee will find it mature enough, and how it would handle the Bergemann-Morris attribution.
Uncertain breadth of real-world implementation compared with other candidates.
